title: Article 315 — Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States

content.overview: Article 315 — Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States. Complete constitutional treatise with procedural anchors, cases, and chamber drafting blueprints.
content.study:
Topic at a Glance
Article 315 of the Constitution of India is titled “Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States”. It forms an integral component of Services under the Union and the States (Articles 308–323), located within the “Services” cluster. Current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023.

Constitutional Text & Anatomy
(1) Subject to the provisions of this article, there shall be a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State.

(2) Two or more States may agree that there shall be one Public Service Commission for that group of States, and if a resolution to that effect is passed by the House or, where there are two Houses, by each House of the Legislature of each of those States, Parliament may by law provide for the appointment of a Joint State Public Service Commission (referred to in this Chapter as Joint Commission) to serve the needs of those States.

(3) Any such law as aforesaid may contain such incidental and consequential provisions as may be necessary or desirable for giving effect to the purposes of the law.

(4) The Public Service Commission for the Union, if requested so to do by the Governor 1 [omitted of a State, may, with the approval of the President, agree to serve all or any of the needs of the State.

(5) References in this Constitution to the Union Public Service Commission or a State Public Service Commission shall, unless the context otherwise requires, be construed as references to the Commission serving the needs of the Union or, as the case may be, the State as respects the particular matter in question.

Constituent Assembly Intent & Doctrinal Foundation
The framers envisioned Article 315 as a fundamental structural instrument. In constitutional jurisprudence, every clause operates not in isolation but as part of an integrated, transformative organic document. It regulates executive, legislative, or fundamental citizen interests to maintain the rule of law and constitutional supremacy.

Procedural & Courtroom Anchors (Senior Counsel Checklist)
1. Competent Forum: High Court under Article 226 (judicial review of legislative and executive action, challenge to vires) and Supreme Court under Article 136 (Special Leave Petition) / Article 32 (if fundamental rights are violated).
2. Standard of Review: Ultra vires doctrine, legislative competence (Lists I, II, III of Seventh Schedule), non-arbitrariness under Article 14, and procedural vires.
3. Standing & Remedial Path: Aggrieved party whose legal, statutory, or constitutional rights are infringed, or public-spirited person in representative actions where public interest is directly affected.
4. Evidentiary Standards: Where disputed facts or legislative arbitrariness are alleged, evidentiary burdens under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA ss. 104–106) and official gazette notifications govern the record.

Key Statutory Ingredients to Establish
1. (1) Subject to the provisions of this article, there shall be a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State.
2. (2) Two or more States may agree that there shall be one Public Service Commission for that group of States, and if a resolution to that effect is passed by the House or, where there are two Houses, by each House of the Legislature of each of those States, Parliament may by law provide for the appointment of a Joint State Public Service Commission (referred to in this Chapter as Joint Commission) to serve the needs of those States.
3. (3) Any such law as aforesaid may contain such incidental and consequential provisions as may be necessary or desirable for giving effect to the purposes of the law.
4. (4) The Public Service Commission for the Union, if requested so to do by the Governor 1 [omitted of a State, may, with the approval of the President, agree to serve all or any of the needs of the State.
5. (5) References in this Constitution to the Union Public Service Commission or a State Public Service Commission shall, unless the context otherwise requires, be construed as references to the Commission serving the needs of the Union or, as the case may be, the State as respects the particular matter in question.

Judicial Interpretation & Binding Ratios
1. Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) (1973) 4 SCC 225: The Constitution is the supreme law of the land; constitutional provisions must be harmoniously construed to preserve its basic structure and core institutional balance.
2. Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980) (1980) 3 SCC 625: Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles form the bedrock of the Constitution; institutional boundaries and constitutional discipline cannot be breached.

Current-Law Position & Milestone
Current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023. Any attempt by subordinate legislation or executive notifications to abridge the mandate of Article 315 is subject to judicial review under Articles 226 and 32.
